title: eBook | How can utilities and developers make confident investment decisions in an increasingly complex US power market?
gist: A Wood Mackenzie eBook landing page arguing that US utilities and developers face demand uncertainty from AI, data centres, electrification and industrial expansion, and that national forecasts miss the local interconnection, policy and supply chain constraints that decide project viability. The page is promotional gated marketing rather than analysis; its only substantive content is a six-capability decision framework (foresight, integration, precision, speed, defensibility, resilience).

insights.claim: AI and data centre growth, electrification and industrial expansion are jointly reshaping US electricity demand, leaving open where that demand materialises and which infrastructure serves it.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Frames the three demand vectors utilities and developers must size before committing capital.
insights.quote: AI and data centre growth, electrification and industrial expansion are reshaping US electricity demand.
insights.locator: AI and data centre growth, electrification

insights.claim: National US power demand forecasts only tell part of the story because local market dynamics, interconnection availability, infrastructure constraints, policy and generation mix can dramatically change the outlook for individual markets and projects.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Argues that node-level rather than national demand data is the analytical edge in siting US power assets.
insights.quote: National forecasts only tell part of the story.
insights.locator: Can you identify where power demand will materialise?

insights.claim: Choosing what and where to build now requires evaluating demand growth alongside transmission access, interconnection availability, regulatory support, technology economics and infrastructure readiness simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A six-variable siting checklist for screening US generation projects before capital commitment.
insights.quote: Choosing what and where to build increasingly means evaluating demand growth alongside transmission access, interconnection availability, regulatory support, technology economics and infrastructure readiness.
insights.locator: Are you investing in the right assets, in the right locations?

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie positions multi-scenario assessment - rather than a single base case - as the method for power investment planning under demand uncertainty.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Scenario-based capital allocation is the stated planning norm; single-forecast underwriting is treated as inadequate.
insights.locator: The ebook explores how utilities and developers

insights.claim: Equipment shortages, tariffs, manufacturing constraints and long lead times can materially affect US power project costs and delivery schedules.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Procurement risk, not demand risk, may be the near-term determinant of project IRR - stress-test lead times and tariff exposure.
insights.quote: Equipment shortages, tariffs, manufacturing constraints and long lead times can materially affect project costs and delivery schedules.
insights.locator: Could supply chain constraints derail your plans?

insights.claim: Developers are advised to anticipate supply chain bottlenecks and stress-test procurement assumptions before constraints threaten project viability, treating execution risk as a pre-FID screen.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Pushes procurement diligence upstream into the investment decision rather than the build phase.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie identifies six capabilities as critical for power sector decision-makers: foresight, integration, precision, speed, defensibility and resilience.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A named vendor framework worth filing as the diligence rubric utilities are being sold on.
insights.quote: the six capabilities Wood Mackenzie identifies as critical for power sector decision-makers: foresight, integration, precision, speed, defensibility and resilience
insights.locator: Make better power investment decisions under uncertainty

insights.claim: The pitch is that connecting demand intelligence, investment planning and supply chain insight in one view produces faster and more defensible decisions than treating them separately.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Signals where commercial energy-data vendors are converging - integrated intelligence products rather than standalone forecasts.
insights.quote: connect demand intelligence, investment planning and supply chain insight to make faster, more defensible decisions
